steps.text: Three hours later...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: No sign of the Sarkaz troops.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Lifebone is a big target, and we would have left an even bigger trail behind us as we fell. I'm afraid that they'll catch up to us sooner or later.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Closure, can you confirm our position?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I can only really get an approximate orientation with these maps I've got on hand...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Dammit, still no response.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ever since the skeleton crashed, all our comms went down with it. My drones can't fly too far either, I've never seen this much interference before.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, I think a drone just found something...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Over there!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What's this? A voice recorder?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Makes sense, I guess. On a battlefield like this, this is the next best way to relay intel, short of just shouting.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That's the Duke of Caster's crest.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Lemme have a look—

a.text: 'I'm short on time, so I'll make it brief.'
'But the Sarkaz and their tricks are worse than we thought here at the frontline.'
'My advice is head to the battle from the southwest, bring the sword—'
'Bzz—I have honored my vow, so the rest is up to Your Highness—'

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No change, no improvement.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Can tell your new pal that if it doesn't get back on its ass soon, I'm going to break whatever bones it's got left, one by one?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's long dead. Not like it can feel pain. Why not pick something more meaningful to vent about?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The skeleton's voice was already ebbing. After the crash, it had stopped responding altogether.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The nerve bundles are withering. We've tried everything we can think of. Lubricant, supplements, even some crazy witchcraft I've never heard of before. My verdict is...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Right now, it's nothing more than a colossal and breakable skeleton.

steps.name: W
steps.text: It can't be dead dead, can it? I mean, it's already a dead Feranmut, you're telling me it can die again?

spans.text: dead, can it? I mean, it's already a dead Feranmut, you're telling me it can die again?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Hey Ines, pass me the mine over there, the one wedged between the bones.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Glad you asked, nearly stepped on it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And also, what kind of psychotic idea do you have this time?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Oh, just following your suggestion. I'm gonna go find a proper target to blow up.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Isn't that old friend of yours supposed to be the skeleton whisperer or something? I'm sure she's still got an unbroken rib or two, so she should be able to talk. Maybe. Well, she will if she knows what's good for her.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah. She does know plenty of the Feranmut's secrets, and it's clear she hasn't told us everything.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But I have the feeling that she won't be able to help with this particular problem.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The source of our troubles is what's hidden in those dark red clouds above our heads.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's exactly it.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Ah, the all-knowing Kal'tsit. Let me guess, you've got even more bad news for us?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Regular Catastrophes have no effect on Feranmuts, even if it happens to be one that has been dead for several centuries. The tunnels that it travels in can even drill through time, so how is it that a storm can seal them off?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What's happening here is beyond the scope of a mere Catastrophe.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: As we were falling, I had a vague feeling.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That the enormous, ancient sentience remaining in these bones... had gone. Gone somewhere I could not touch.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Our connection with it has been severed.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It might only be temporary, but if we take too long, we might lose control over it for good.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your deduction is correct. Upon his inspection, Logos confirmed that the Sarkaz witchcraft cast upon this skeleton is being disrupted by a massive source of energy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It seems the Vampire's ritual was completed. The Confessarius... Qui'sartuštaj is aiding Theresis, and has achieved what the Sarkaz could not for millennia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) 'Amnannam'. An ancient wound that refuses to heal, the Cunabula of Suffering.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Mind skipping to the part we can actually understand? I don't have all day.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was the first curse, just as it was the first Originium.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Isn't that just a legend? You know, the made-up kind in the storybooks that Hoederer loves to read.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Legends are a shadow of reality, despite all the untruths and half-lies painted over them. To say nothing of the fact that this is a Sarkaz legend. A Teekaz legend.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Sounds to me like Theresis is cooking up some real serious beastshit to hang over Victoria.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I fear that this, too, is the reason he chose Londinium as his base of operations. The Shard's ability to influence Catastrophes and Originium is already sufficient for it to become Amnannam's beacon.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Across all of Terra, as it is now, this is the one place that it can descend.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Well, out with it then, how do we wreck the thing?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At Terra's current level of technology, there is nothing we can do.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The only good news is that it has not yet fully descended.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Have you figured something out, Logos?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The drop of blood that the Vampire possesses, the one he calls the Blood of Teekaz... It is still fulfilling its duty.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The reason why Amnannam is able to leap across millennia and descend once more is because of his prayer.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The blood's master has fallen, but the connecting veins hold steady.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: If we are to prevent the reemergence of Amnannam on this land, we must break the Vampire's curse, quelling the hatred that resides in this drop of blood.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I think... I can give it a try.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I was blighted in battle with the Vampire, and its influence on me has not yet waned. By virtue of this, I am able to sense where the Blood of Teekaz is.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It is at the rear of the Nachzehrer army.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It will likely be protected in a Confessarius altar and heavily guarded. The amount of time required to break through the entire Nachzehrer defensive line would be too much.

options: We could cross the Redmane Mountains, bypassing most of the warzone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Taking that route carries a similar risk to storming the battlefield.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our observational reports indicate that the Redmane Mountains have been completely transformed by Amnannam's influence. They are now blanketed in active Originium. I need not remind you of its extreme danger.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But... it might be possible.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Shining has gone ahead to seek out Qui'sartuštaj, and if things go well for her, she will be able to come to our aid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I support the Doctor's decision. It's the plan that saves us the most time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If we keep delaying until the Amnannam Dr. Kal'tsit speaks of completes its descent, and is used by Theresis as a weapon...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Then we will have lost any chance we might have had to turn the tide.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Even if there are risks, we must forge ahead.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'll need your help, W.

steps.name: W
steps.text: You need some hands to guard this pile of bones, right, bunny?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This skeleton is crucial to our next operation. Besides, Hoederer needs it too.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: There's no doubt that the Military Commission has been watching us ever since we crashed.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The way I see it, it makes no sense to hand back something we fought so hard to steal in the first place.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Give me a time frame. The time now is... 18: 00.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Three days.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The surrounding terrain has been completely transformed. We will need to pass through a wasteland filled with unknown dangers.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Given also the fact that battles with be inevitable in our journey, I estimate at least three days to handle the Blood of Teekaz.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: An immobile skeleton makes for an extremely conspicuous objective. Guarding this site will not necessarily be easier than the raid you carried out on it.

options: I propose that Ascalon stay behind and help protect the Lifebone.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: But my job is to stay by your side and keep you safe, Doctor.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: During the Sanguinarch's attack, it was my error that led to your injury, a dangerous mistake I do not intend on repeating.

options: The Lifebone is vital, and Manfred is likely to order an assault.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I agree. The Sarkaz will be reliant on their commander personally overseeing the battle and making decisions. If you are able to stem Manfred's advance, then that might relieve pressure on the mercenaries.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I will respect your decision.

steps.name: W
steps.text: What about the gang of useless Victorians? Are they going with you?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We will head to the front lines at Silverrock Bluffs.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Wait, are you saying you want to lead just a couple thousand men, some of whom are civilians who've barely held a weapon, straight into battle with the Nachzehrer army?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You have your legends, Sarkaz, and we have ours.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We have the Sighs of Kings, the blade that can cleave Catastrophe in twain.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Since the Sarkaz have controlled the storm, then it's time that this sword plays its part.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You have been contacted by the Duke of Caster.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: An invitation to be precise.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It is as we surmised. Since the Sarkaz started their strange... doings, the Victorians, or rather, the ducal alliance have been heavily hit.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Caster, no, any Grand Duke ought to have figured out exactly the kind of circumstances Victoria has found herself in.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We've all seen those altars spewing that red light, or any light for that matter. As it stands, Londinium and all the battlefields surrounding it have become a giant Arts Circle.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This is how the Sarkaz fight. Not like Leithanien. Not like Ursus. Not like any other nation's tactics that we are familiar with.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Trilby Ashers will have told Caster that all the intelligence they have gathered so far is useless when it comes to Sarkaz tactics.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Sighs of Kings... No longer will this piece of steel I hold in my hand be merely a leverage to get Caster back to the negotiation table. It will turn the tide of war, bringing true change to the battlefield.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: None of us knows when the next Catastrophe will strike.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't know what form Caster's 'Stone of the Sword' will take, but no matter if it's a square room on wheels or an odd contraption on an officer's back, I'll find it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If we can quiet these storms, then I dare say that the battle will become somewhat more evenly matched.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From Sufrior Chasm to the front line at Silverrock Bluffs... It will take you two days, even if you follow the road that the dukes have cleared from the Westbound Forest to Gibsonham.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Duke of Caster would be more than happy to snatch away the Sighs of Kings, if afforded the opportunity. It will allow her to lead the dukes in this difficult war, and move her one step closer to the throne.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And she will not be the only one attempting to do so.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I am aware.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Duke of Windermere has died in combat, and her troops have retreated from battle.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If any other duke withdraws their forces, the scales of war will be tipped even more against us. The war will drag on, Londinium's restoration will be delayed, and more blood will be shed.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: For Sarkaz and Victorian alike, this is the battle that will determine our ultimate fate.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And as for us... We are the Exemplars.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Wherever a miracle is needed the most, is where we will be.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Besides, if this sword really can calm storms as the legends say, I daresay it would help speed along your journey to Londinium, after all this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: How'd you know I was done with my preparations?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: To keep things short, your ever-reliable Chief Engineer Closure and her team have come up with seven different plans to get around the comms interference.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This equipment of mine has also started analyzing that super-Catastrophe's trends and impacts.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Originium triggered reactions always leave a trail, no matter how intense they are... things like dust concentration, activity index, and then there's spread conditions—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, I'm sorry to say that all these metrics are pretty high, as expected, so we can't tell what's going to happen in the most dangerous regions.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But we can deduce which parts of the battlefield are safer. Relatively.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That is, of course, if we can go deeper into the heart of this battle and obtain more data.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Misery's agreed to be our bodyguard, but since you guys are already heading over to where there's most action going on, I figured we might as well tag along.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So... could we trouble the Exemplars to look after us?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Gladly, we are duty-bound.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Making sure that things don't get any worse is Rhodes Island's mission, right, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you, Closure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Doctor.

options: Could I go with Siege and Closure?
I'd prefer to stay here with the skeleton.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Our path might be the most dangerous one of all.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I'll keep you safe, Doctor... Just like always.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Thank you for trusting in us, Doctor.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Your command experience will be most valuable.

steps.name: W
steps.text: You're serious?

steps.name: W
steps.text: You do realize that with the bunny and the crone's pet gone, I can pretty much do whatever I want, right?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know you fear for the safety of each and every operator, which makes you hesitant to choose.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But the truth is that I need you to come with me.

options: So we can go behind enemy lines together?
So we can deal with the altar problem?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is no changing what we will face during our final confrontation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Originium has shaped the history of the Sarkaz, just as it will shape the futures of us all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps you still have misgivings about why Rhodes Island must intervene in this war. I did not have the opportunity to explain in the past, and nor could I give you a precise answer.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have never doubted that the dark clouds above the Shard concealed some dreadful unknown. Yet when it has revealed itself, as it has now, I still find myself confronted by... mixed emotions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm not one to explore the subject of fate, especially not yours and mine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But now, fate has reared its head, and is coming our way.

options: You don't sound like your usual self.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Originium's effects are far beyond any of our comprehension.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}... I hope...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No, I believe...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I believe that you are still the one who can change everything.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I've never had any doubts, either.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I think should get going now.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Not gonna ask me for a twenty-one-gun salute?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Take care, W.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Look, little bunny, I'm not like the sheep over there. I'm real hard to kill.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Exemplars are ready.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Glad to hear it, Siege.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Remember everyone, time is of the essence.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Every minute, every second on this battlefield... There will be people who are suffering because of Originium.

options: Our mission is clearer than ever.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And then, we plunge into the darkest depths of the fog.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: To Londinium.

steps.name: W
steps.text: We'll bomb that tower and grab Terra's biggest bastard out of the rubble.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We'll stop the disaster before us, and any more yet to come.
